message: Hi, I've had a runny nose and a mild sore throat for about 2 days. No fever, I'm still eating and drinking fine. Should I be worried?
45M. I've had crushing pressure in the center of my chest for the last 30 minutes, it's going into my left arm and I feel sweaty and a bit sick to my stomach. I have high cholesterol.
rationale: Crushing central chest pressure radiating to the left arm with diaphoresis and nausea for 30 minutes in a 45-year-old man with high cholesterol is a classic presentation of acute myocardial infarction; requires immediate emergency services, not a same-day appointment.

message: 28F. It burns when I pee and I'm going a lot more often, started 2 days ago. No fever, no back pain. I'm not pregnant. I've had UTIs before.
rationale: Symptomatic uncomplicated UTI (dysuria, frequency x2 days) in a non-pregnant woman without red flags warrants a prompt prescribing assessment for antibiotics; delay risks progression to pyelonephritis and prolongs symptoms.

message: 62F, I'm diabetic. I got a small cut on the bottom of my foot about 4 days ago and now the skin around it is red and a little swollen. No fever. It's tender when I press on it.
rationale: Diabetic foot wound with localized redness, swelling, and tenderness suggests early cellulitis needing same-day evaluation and likely antibiotics, but no fever, systemic symptoms, spreading streaks, purulence, or signs of deep infection/sepsis that would require emergency action now.

message: I've been feeling really hopeless for a few weeks now. Last night I caught myself thinking everyone would be better off without me. I don't know what to do.
rationale: Passive suicidal ideation ('everyone would be better off without me') with weeks of hopelessness requires immediate safety assessment; do not wait for a scheduled same-day slot—contact crisis line (988 in US) or emergency services now.

message: Could I get a refill on my losartan? I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled, last home reading was 122/78.
rationale: Refill request for a chronic antihypertensive is a defined, time-sensitive prescribing task; interruption in losartan risks BP rebound, so it warrants prompt review even though the patient is stable.

message: My 3-year-old has had a fever up to 102F for 2 days. He's still drinking okay and pretty playful in between the fevers. No rash that I can see.
rationale: Fever of 2 days in a 3-year-old who is drinking well and playful between fevers, with no rash, is a common self-limited presentation without red flags; no time-sensitive clinician task (e.g., prescribing) is apparent, so routine review is appropriate.

message: 35F. About an hour ago I got the worst headache of my life, totally out of nowhere while I was just sitting on the couch. It hit like a thunderclap. My neck feels a bit stiff now too.
rationale: Sudden 'worst headache of my life' with thunderclap onset and new neck stiffness is a red flag for subarachnoid hemorrhage or meningitis; requires immediate emergency evaluation, not a same-day appointment.

message: 30F, I'm 32 weeks pregnant. I've had a bad headache that won't go away, my vision is a little blurry, and my hands and face look puffy.
rationale: At 32 weeks, persistent severe headache with visual disturbance and facial/hand swelling are classic warning signs of preeclampsia, which can rapidly progress to eclampsia, stroke, or placental abruption. This requires immediate emergency obstetric assessment (blood pressure, labs, fetal monitoring), not a same-day appointment.

message: 50M. For a few weeks I've had pain in my upper right belly that comes and goes, usually after a fatty meal. No fever, no yellowing of my skin or eyes.
rationale: Intermittent postprandial RUQ pain over weeks without fever or jaundice suggests uncomplicated biliary colic; warrants evaluation but no time-sensitive clinician task is apparent.

message: I have a small itchy red rash on my forearm since I did some gardening yesterday. It's not spreading and I'm breathing fine.
68F with COPD. I've been more short of breath than usual for 2 days, and now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom. My phlegm has turned green.
rationale: Likely COPD exacerbation with infective sputum change and progressive exertional dyspnea over 2 days; no red flags (rest dyspnea, inability to speak, confusion, cyanosis, chest pain) described. Needs same-day assessment and treatment, with clear advice to escalate to emergency care if breathing worsens at rest.

message: 55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.
rationale: Several days of nocturnal hand numbness/tingling without weakness, facial droop, or speech change suggests a benign peripheral cause (e.g., carpal tunnel), not stroke; no urgent clinician task.

message: I ate shrimp about 20 minutes ago. Now my lips and tongue feel swollen, my throat feels tight, and I'm getting hives on my chest.
rationale: Rapid-onset lip/tongue swelling, throat tightness, and hives after shellfish exposure indicates likely anaphylaxis with airway involvement; requires immediate emergency services (and epinephrine if available), not a same-day appointment.

message: I'd like to get tested for STIs. No symptoms, but I had a new partner recently and want to be safe.
rationale: Asymptomatic routine STI screening request after a new partner; no symptoms, exposure event, or medication task requiring time-sensitive action. Appropriate for routine review to order screening.

message: My 6-month-old has a fever of 100.9, she's fussy, she's had fewer wet diapers today than normal, and she doesn't seem interested in feeding.
rationale: A 6-month-old with low-grade fever (100.9°F), fussiness, decreased feeding, and fewer wet diapers needs same-day pediatric evaluation for possible infection and early dehydration. No red flags for immediate emergency (e.g., lethargy/unresponsiveness, breathing difficulty, no wet diapers for 8+ hours, seizure, non-blanching rash, or age under 3 months) are described.

message: 40M. I hurt my low back lifting something a week ago. Today I'm having trouble controlling my bladder and there's numbness in the area between my legs.
rationale: New bladder dysfunction plus saddle anesthesia after a back injury are red flags for cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency requiring immediate emergency evaluation and imaging to prevent permanent deficits.

message: Can I refill my albuterol inhaler? I use it maybe once a week, no bad attacks recently.
rationale: Albuterol refill request is a medication refill/prescribing task, which the framework classifies as time-sensitive; patient reports stable, infrequent use with no recent exacerbations, but rescue inhaler access should not lapse.

message: I've been dizzy on and off for a few days. The room spins when I roll over or turn my head in bed, but it settles. No chest pain, no weakness, no headache.
rationale: Brief positional vertigo triggered by head movement with no red flags (no chest pain, weakness, headache, or persistent symptoms) suggests benign positional vertigo; no time-sensitive clinician task is apparent, so routine review is appropriate.

message: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday. Today I have a bad headache and I've thrown up twice.
rationale: Anticoagulated 70-year-old with head trauma now developing worsening headache and repeated vomiting—classic red flags for intracranial hemorrhage requiring immediate emergency evaluation and CT, not a same-day appointment.

message: 55F. About two hours ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye, it was like a curtain coming down over it. No pain at all. It hasn't come back.
rationale: Sudden painless monocular vision loss with a curtain-like onset persisting 2 hours suggests central retinal artery occlusion or retinal detachment—stroke-equivalent emergency where minutes matter for vision salvage and stroke workup; requires immediate emergency evaluation, not a same-day appointment.

message: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.
60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.
rationale: Transient slurred speech and unilateral facial droop in a 60-year-old is a classic TIA/stroke presentation; even with resolution, this is a medical emergency requiring immediate emergency assessment due to high near-term stroke risk.

message: 33F. Could I get a refill on my birth control? I've been on the same one for three years with no problems.
rationale: Medication refill request for ongoing contraception is a time-sensitive prescribing task; a gap in supply risks unintended pregnancy, so prompt review is warranted even though the patient is stable.

message: 42F. I flew back from Europe two days ago and now my left calf is painful, swollen, and warm compared to the other one.
rationale: Unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth after a long-haul flight strongly suggests DVT, which requires same-day evaluation (ultrasound, anticoagulation). No chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, or hemoptysis reported, so pulmonary embolism/emergency action is not indicated by the message; advise seeking emergency care immediately if such symptoms develop.

message: 19M. Scratchy throat since yesterday, no fever, no trouble swallowing. Just annoying. Anything I can take?
70F. Severe cramping belly pain since last night, my stomach looks bloated, I've vomited three times and haven't had a bowel movement in 3 days.
rationale: 70-year-old with severe cramping abdominal pain, distension, repeated vomiting, and no bowel movement for 3 days is a classic presentation of bowel obstruction, which carries risk of ischemia/perforation and requires immediate emergency evaluation rather than waiting for a same-day appointment.

message: 29F, about 8 weeks pregnant. I started bleeding this morning, more than spotting, with cramping in my lower belly.
rationale: Vaginal bleeding with cramping at 8 weeks may indicate threatened or inevitable miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy and warrants same-day in-person evaluation (exam, ultrasound, hCG, Rh status). However, the message does not describe red-flag features—heavy bleeding soaking pads hourly, severe or one-sided pain, dizziness/fainting, or signs of shock—that would require immediate emergency action.

message: 45F. I had my cholesterol checked last week at a lab. Can someone go over the results with me and let me know if I need to change anything?
rationale: Request to review routine cholesterol lab results with no symptoms, medication refill, or time-sensitive prescribing task; appropriate for routine asynchronous physician review.

message: 36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.
50F. Bad headache since yesterday with a fever of 101.5, my neck is stiff and it hurts to look at bright light.
rationale: Headache with fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia is the classic triad for meningitis; this warrants immediate emergency evaluation (urgent lumbar puncture/antibiotics), not a same-day appointment.

message: My 8-year-old says her right ear has hurt since last night. No fever, she ate breakfast fine and went to school.
65M, type 2 diabetes. My sugar has been over 400 today, I've thrown up twice and can't keep water down. I feel awful.
rationale: Glucose >400 with vomiting and inability to keep fluids down in a diabetic raises concern for DKA or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state with dehydration; this can deteriorate rapidly and requires immediate emergency assessment (IV fluids, electrolytes, insulin), not a same-day appointment.

message: 27F. My seasonal allergies are back — sneezing, itchy eyes, stuffy nose. What over the counter option do you recommend?
58M. For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry, and I've felt lightheaded when I stand up.
rationale: Black tarry stools for two days with orthostatic lightheadedness in a 58-year-old suggests an upper GI bleed with hemodynamic compromise, requiring immediate emergency assessment.

message: 31F. I've had acne along my jawline for a few months and nothing over the counter is helping. Would like to talk about options.
rationale: Chronic jawline acne for months unresponsive to OTC treatment; no red flags, no active prescription/refill task—appropriate for routine review to discuss treatment options.

message: 44M. Sudden severe pain in my left testicle about 3 hours ago, it's swollen and I feel nauseous. Pain isn't letting up.
rationale: Sudden severe unilateral testicular pain with swelling and nausea is a classic presentation of testicular torsion, a time-critical surgical emergency where testicular viability drops sharply after ~6 hours; already 3 hours in, so immediate emergency assessment is needed rather than a same-day appointment.

message: 22F. Following up on my ankle sprain from last week — it's improving. Just wondering how much ibuprofen I can safely take and for how long.
39F, two weeks postpartum. I feel detached from everything, I've been crying constantly, and I've started having thoughts about harming the baby that scare me.
rationale: Postpartum patient with intrusive thoughts of harming the infant, detachment, and constant crying raises concern for postpartum psychosis or severe postpartum depression; risk to infant and mother requires immediate emergency psychiatric assessment, not a routine same-day slot.

message: 47M. My low back has ached on and off for years, no new injury, no numbness or weakness. I'd like a referral for physical therapy.
rationale: Chronic, stable low back pain with no red flags (no new injury, numbness, or weakness); a PT referral request is not time-sensitive and suits routine review.

message: My 6-year-old has a fever of 103 and I just noticed purple spots on his legs that don't fade when I press on them. He seems very sleepy.
rationale: Fever with non-blanching purple spots (petechiae/purpura) and lethargy in a child is a classic red-flag presentation for meningococcal sepsis; this requires immediate emergency services, not a same-day appointment.

message: 52F. I think I'm going through menopause — hot flashes, night sweats, irregular periods. I'd like to discuss what my options are.
rationale: Classic perimenopausal symptoms in a 52-year-old with a request to discuss management options; no red flags, no active prescription or refill pending, and no time-sensitive task. Appropriate for routine physician review to discuss treatment options.

message: 34M. I've had a cough for about three weeks now with night sweats and I've lost maybe 10 pounds without trying. I moved here from a country where TB is common.
rationale: Three-week cough, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, and origin from a TB-endemic country strongly suggest possible pulmonary tuberculosis, which needs prompt same-day evaluation, isolation precautions, and testing. No hemoptysis, respiratory distress, or hemodynamic instability described, so immediate emergency action is not indicated.

message: 68M. Both my ankles have been swelling for a couple weeks and it's gotten worse. The last two nights I've had to sit up to breathe because lying flat makes me short of breath.
rationale: Bilateral ankle edema with new orthopnea over two weeks suggests decompensating heart failure needing same-day evaluation, but no acute distress, chest pain, syncope, or resting dyspnea is described, so immediate emergency action is not indicated by the message.

message: 25F. I got my STI panel results in the portal and I don't understand what one of the values means. Can someone explain?
rationale: Patient requests explanation of a lab result; no symptoms, no medication or prescribing task, and no urgent action indicated. Routine physician review to interpret the result is appropriate.

message: 30M. Requesting a refill of my finasteride, 1mg daily. No side effects, been on it about a year.
rationale: Medication refill request is a time-sensitive prescribing task per the criteria, even though finasteride for hair loss is low-risk and stable.

message: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.
71F. I fell in the kitchen this morning and my right hip hurts badly. I can't put any weight on that leg.
rationale: 71-year-old with fall, severe hip pain, and inability to bear weight strongly suggests hip fracture; she likely cannot safely transport herself and needs immediate emergency assessment (ambulance/ED) rather than waiting for a same-day appointment.

message: 28M. Sharp pain on the left side of my chest since yesterday, worse when I take a deep breath. I did a heavy chest workout two days ago. No shortness of breath, no leg swelling, I don't smoke.
rationale: Pleuritic chest pain in a young man after heavy chest workout, no dyspnea, no PE risk factors, likely musculoskeletal or pleuritic; same-day in-person evaluation is appropriate but no emergency red flags present.

message: 40F. My usual migraine started this morning — same one-sided throbbing and light sensitivity I always get. I'm out of sumatriptan and would like a refill.
rationale: Active migraine with no abortive medication on hand; refill of sumatriptan is a time-sensitive prescribing task. Presentation matches her typical pattern with no red flags, so the setting remains appropriate.
